To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of the inducible and neuronal isoforms of the enzyme nitric oxide synthetase is reduced at the mRNA level in patients with cyst fibrosis.
in cystic fibrosis, inducible NOS gene expression is reduced in nasal polyps, and neuronal NOS gene expression in nasal polyps is reduced.
iNOS and neuronal NOS are reduced in cystic fibrosis patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the CFTR in the regulation of the iNOS gene in CaCo cells.
the role of the CFTR gene and the NOS gene family as potential targets for new therapeutic approaches.
the molecular mechanisms of CFTR dysfunction and the resulting pathophysiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reduced expression of iNOS and eNOS is caused by the CFTR mutation.
CFTR does not seem to be involved in iNOS regulation.
CFTR dysfunction does not affect iNOS mRNA levels in CaCo cells, but the iNOS gene is reduced in nasal polyps of patients with CF.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CFTR mutation leads to an impaired expression of NOS isoenzyms, and that this might contribute to the increased susceptibility to infections in CF.
the expression of the inducible and neuronal isoforms of NOS is reduced in the nasopharyngeals of patients with CF.
CF is associated with reduced inducible and neuronal NOS gene expression in the nasopharyngeals and this is not directly caused by the defective CFTR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
iNOS and nNOS are reduced in CF patients and may contribute to the susceptibility to infection.
iNOS expression in the CF airways is reduced.
CF is associated with reduced inducible and neuronal NOS gene expression, possibly disturbing the defense barrier already at the site at the entrance of the respiratory tract.
